solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Home, well-behaved? Something believed sincerely (2,4,5)

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home

annotation.surface: Someone checks that home life is orderly and that their beliefs are sincerely held.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is only the last word; 'Something believed sincerely' reads as one phrase, but 'sincerely' breaks off to define the whole answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Acting in good faith means acting honestly and sincerely.

entries.clue: Expecting popular pupils? Half missing! (2,3)

indicatorNotes.Half missing: half of the word is missing, so only three of its six letters remain

blocks.note: PUPILS with its second half (ILS) gone

annotation.surface: A teacher expecting a crowded classroom finds half the pupils absent.
annotation.walkthrough: IN PUP is said of a pregnant dog, so 'Expecting' is a fair definition even though the surface is about a school.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a pregnant dog, and 'expecting' is the everyday euphemism for pregnant.

entries.clue: Expert in soil — go get changed (9)

indicatorNotes.changed: the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, used again from the definition

annotation.surface: Someone is told to fetch the soil expert and get changed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soil' does double duty: it finishes the definition and also supplies four letters of the fodder, which 'go get' alone cannot fill.
annotation.definitionFit: A geologist studies rocks and soils.

entries.clue: Working in relation to tax (2,4)

blocks.note: the first sense: at one's post, as a nurse on a shift is
ON = about, DUTY = a tax, as on imported goods

annotation.surface: A line from a tax office: working on matters of tax.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase literally: 'on' as in 'a talk on', and a duty is a tax.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for being at one's post, as a nurse or guard is; read literally it is a phrase about a levy on goods.

entries.clue: As you say, gosh, not many here! (3)

indicatorNotes.As you say: the letters come from how the word is spoken

blocks.note: phew is an exclamation like gosh

annotation.surface: Someone surveys an almost empty room and exclaims how few people came.
annotation.walkthrough: PHEW and FEW sound the same; the exclamation mark belongs to the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small number, as in 'a handful turned up'.

entries.clue: Initially irritated, rising uproar about drink, tasteless (7)

indicatorNotes.Initially: what comes initially in a word is its first letter, so only the I of irritated is used
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising reads the word from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.about: the reversed word goes around the drink

blocks.note: a sip is a small drink; it goes inside N…ID

annotation.surface: An irritated customer makes a fuss over a bland drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The drink sits between the N and the ID of the upturned DIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink has no flavour.

entries.clue: New court rule hit garden business (12)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters form a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A new court ruling has hurt the garden centre trade.
annotation.walkthrough: The legal surface hides that all twelve letters are there to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: The science and trade of growing plants, fruit and flowers, which is what nurseries and garden centres live by.

entries.clue: Bold porter regularly displaying extravagance (12)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: every other one

blocks.note: P, R and E: the first, third and fifth letters of porter
something sumptuous is lavish, displaying extravagance

annotation.surface: A cheeky hotel porter shows off expensive tastes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bold' here means cheeky or forward, not brave.
annotation.definitionFit: Presumptuous behaviour is overbold, taking liberties.

entries.clue: Feature of parachute drop starts to cause regular injuries unfortunately (3,4)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starts, or first letters, of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.unfortunately: the letters end up in an unlucky, jumbled order

blocks.note: first letters of cause, regular, injuries

annotation.surface: A warning that parachute drops regularly cause injuries.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parachute drop' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'parachute' and 'drop' joins the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The ripcord is the cord pulled to open a parachute.

entries.clue: Wife is extremely eager, extra shrewd (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of eager

annotation.surface: A wife is described as very keen and extra clever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like it intensifies 'eager' and instead takes its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative: 'extra' does the work of the -ER ending, and wise and shrewd are close synonyms.

entries.clue: Was a fan of fantastic Reds up top (9)

annotation.surface: A football fan used to follow a brilliant Reds side at the top of the league.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reds' suggests a football team (Liverpool or Manchester United), which is the scene: the answer is what a fan did.
annotation.definitionFit: The British sporting sense: a fan follows and backs a club, and the past tense matches 'Was'.

entries.clue: Small drink at first for writer (9)

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

annotation.surface: A writer has a small drink first thing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like one phrase meaning initially, but it splits: AT, then 1ST with the numeral as I.
annotation.definitionFit: A playwright is one particular kind of writer, so the definition is a broad category.

entries.clue: Greek character’s quiet greeting (3)

annotation.surface: A Greek person gives a soft hello.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person; the ’s stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A character is a letter, and this is the 21st letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Believer’s arithmetic calculation recalled little interesting maths to begin with (6)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.to begin with: take the first letters of the words before it

blocks.clueFragment: little interesting maths to begin with
blocks.note: first letters of little, interesting, maths

annotation.surface: A believer remembers the maths lessons that first caught their interest.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a follower of Islam is one kind of religious believer.

entries.clue: Newspaper pay increase — everyday event? (7)

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
in Britain a pay rise is a raise

annotation.surface: A newspaper's staff get a pay rise, and wonder whether that will happen every day.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'everyday event' is a playful definition: the sun rises every single day.
annotation.definitionFit: Sunrise happens every morning.

entries.clue: Secure gold in vehicle (6)

blocks.note: to land a deal is to secure it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: Someone locks up gold inside a vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction, but here it only links definition to wordplay; a landau is an old horse-drawn carriage.
annotation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

entries.clue: Leaves Selby carrying vase maybe (6)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the phrase carries the answer inside it

annotation.surface: Someone leaves the Yorkshire town of Selby carrying a vase.
annotation.walkthrough: Selby is a town in North Yorkshire; 'maybe' marks a vase as one example of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A vase is a kind of vessel, a container for liquid.

entries.clue: Money, two notes (3)

blocks.note: the first note: TI, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale (do re mi)
the second note: n., the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote

annotation.surface: A payment made in two banknotes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like banknotes, but one is a note of the scale and the other the abbreviation n. for note; tin is old British slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Tin is dated British slang for money.

entries.clue: Believer in God accepts blame for counsellor (9)

indicatorNotes.accepts: one word takes the other in

blocks.note: to take the rap is to take the blame; it goes inside THE…IST

annotation.surface: A religious believer takes the blame on behalf of a counsellor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Believer in God accepts blame' reads like a confession, but 'accepts' is the container, and the thing taken in is a slang word: to take the rap.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonyms: both are professionals who help clients by talking through their problems.

entries.clue: Island fellow penning one poem (5)

indicatorNotes.penning: the fellow pens, or encloses, the one

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one; it goes inside L…AD

annotation.surface: A man on an island writes a single poem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penning' suggests writing, which suits a poem, but here it means enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War.

entries.clue: Nothing held back wicked girl (5)

annotation.surface: A wicked girl holds nothing back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing held back' reads as a phrase meaning total candour, but the reversal applies to 'wicked'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: crosswords often define a first name just as 'girl' or 'boy', and this is a traditional English girl's name.

entries.clue: Untrustworthy person in shelter after revolution (3)

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind; this word is then turned round

annotation.surface: A traitor hides out in a shelter after a political revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' looks political, and it means a turning round.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the fish is so slippery to hold that its name is used for an evasive, shifty person.

entries.clue: NE Irish broadcast shedding more light? (7)

annotation.surface: A radio programme from the north-east of Ireland explains more about a topic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shedding more light' reads as explaining, and the question mark admits the literal sense: glowing brighter.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: a brighter, glossier surface throws off more light, while 'shedding light' usually means explaining.

entries.clue: Providing strong protection lest pet deal unravels (5-6)

indicatorNotes.unravels: the letters come apart and are rewoven

annotation.surface: An owner wants sturdy protection in case a deal over a pet falls apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: armour of steel plates gives strong protection.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: armour of hard metal sheets is what gives warships and vaults strong protection.
